first_impression.reaction: I googled this half out of curiosity. I haven't decided whether I'm changing my name, but I'd heard marrying overseas complicates it, and that matters because we haven't picked a destination yet. The intro gives me the answer in two short paragraphs: married here, the certificate does it; married overseas, you apply. No 'happily ever after' rubbish. That was enough to keep me reading, at least the overseas and passport parts.

journey.quote: Marry overseas and the picture shifts. NSW and Victoria both say you will need to apply for a change of name.
journey.reaction: This is the line I came for. It changes how we weigh a legal ceremony abroad against signing in Sydney first. Straight to the point.

journey.section: Step 1: Get the official registry marriage certificate (not the ceremonial one)
journey.quote: The handsome certificate you sign at the ceremony is a keepsake.
journey.reaction: I genuinely didn't know that. It's the kind of small insider detail that stops you getting turned away at Service NSW. Useful, and it's said without talking down to me.

journey.section: How to change your name after marriage, step by step
journey.quote: Order is everything here. NSW sets out the sequence plainly: obtain your official marriage certificate, update your driver licence and Medicare card, then change your name everywhere else.
journey.reaction: A clear sequence instead of a giant list. As a lawyer, I like that each step is the proof for the next one.

journey.section: Your options: take, keep, hyphenate or combine
journey.quote: NSW lists three surname options that work with a marriage certificate; every other change, including moving your surname into your middle names, goes through a formal application.
journey.reaction: Accurate, but this whole options section reads like the registry website. I skimmed most of it. Hyphenating is about as far as either of us would go.

journey.section: Changing your name on your passport after marriage
journey.quote: If you were born in Australia and married overseas, it will always need a name change certificate.
journey.reaction: This is what actually affects us. If we marry legally abroad I can't just update my passport when we land, I need the formal change of name first. But the honeymoon would come straight after the wedding, so I'm left piecing the timing together myself. Do I just travel home and on the honeymoon in my current name, and apply later?

journey.section: State by state: NSW, Victoria, Queensland and Western Australia
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the registries agree on the broad shape but word the details differently.
journey.reaction: We're in NSW, so I read that paragraph and skipped the rest. A lot of this repeats the takeaways and the intro. Same point, said three times.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: Bring home the certificate issued where you married, and read how to [get your overseas marriage certificate](https://weddedwonderland.com/expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate) before you leave.
journey.reaction: Practical, and the apostille link after it is the kind of thing I'd never think of until it was too late. This is the section I'd send James.

journey.section: Name change after an overseas or destination wedding
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments as your single point of contact; the name change and every certificate stay with you and the official agencies.
journey.reaction: Honest about where they stop, and I respect that. 'Every certificate stays with you' does make me wonder, though. Does that include the local marriage paperwork at the destination, or only the Australian side? If we marry legally overseas, someone has to deal with the local registry, and I'd want to know whether that's us.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: A fee in writing before any work begins speaks directly to my hidden-costs worry. It's a calm close, not a hard sell.

unanswered_questions: If we marry legally overseas and fly straight to a honeymoon, what is the realistic order: travel on my current passport, then apply for the formal change of name and new passport once we're home?
Roughly how long does a formal NSW change of name take after an overseas marriage, so we know when the new passport is realistic?

When the page says 'every certificate stays with you', does that include the destination's local marriage paperwork and registration, or does the Wedded Advisor coordinate that part with the venue and officiant?
Have you planned a wedding where the couple married legally abroad and dealt with this at home, and can we see it (venue and date)?
would_share_with: James: the 'Name change after an overseas or destination wedding' section, because it's a real point to weigh when we choose between a legal ceremony abroad and signing in Sydney first
Mum: the ceremonial versus official certificate point, because she'll ask

cta_reaction.quote: When the paperwork has a plan, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=name-change-after-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration itself.
cta_reaction.why: It isn't pushy, and it's honest that they handle the celebration rather than the paperwork. But this is admin reading, not inspiration. I'd click to look around, not to enquire. I'd need a couple more posts and a real wedding first.

top_3_changes: In 'Changing your name on your passport after marriage' or the overseas section, add a short plain-English sequence for couples who marry legally abroad and fly to a honeymoon: which passport to travel on, then when to apply for the formal change of name and the new passport. Use only what the Passport Office and NSW already say. Right now I have to piece it together from three paragraphs.
Trim the 'State by state' section where it repeats the intro and takeaways (NSW especially). Keep only what differs by state. As an NSW reader I hit the same point three times and started skimming.

In 'Name change after an overseas or destination wedding', make clear whether 'every certificate stays with you' covers the destination's own marriage paperwork or only the Australian name change. As written, a couple marrying legally abroad can't tell what the Wedded Advisor does on the legal side.
